title: Waymo, robotaxi operators face fresh scrutiny over emergency response failures
slides: Waymo’s robotaxis blocked fire trucks twice. What now?
Emergency response failures triggered a new federal probe.
The real flaw isn’t sensors — it’s coordination with dispatch.
You must verify any fleet’s emergency handoff protocol today.
Test your own city’s interaction with robotaxis this week.
thread_text:
Fire trucks blocked. 

Waymo robotaxis failed to clear a path for emergency vehicles twice in one month, triggering a federal investigation.

Not a sensor issue. 

The real gap is that robotaxis don't talk to emergency dispatch systems in real time.

New probe launched. 

The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration is now auditing Waymo’s emergency response protocols.

Your fleet at risk. 

If your city uses autonomous vehicles, there’s no standard handoff protocol for fire or ambulance calls.

Test this week. 

Call your local fire chief and ask: have your robotaxis ever blocked a response? Run the drill yourself.

script: Call your fire chief this week.

instagram.caption:
Fire trucks were blocked by a self-driving car— twice in one month, and now regulators are stepping in.

Federal investigators just opened a probe into Waymo after its vehicles failed to clear the way for emergency responders. The real gap isn’t better sensors for the cars to “see”—it’s that robotaxis don’t talk to dispatch systems.

If you run a fleet or coordinate with city services, there’s no standard handoff protocol for ambulance or fire calls. That silence can cost minutes.

When was the last time your local fire chief ran a drill with a self-driving car blocking the station driveway? 🚒🛑🔍
